review: 1:3–1:4 שָׁם תָּנוּחַ נַפְשִׁי / כִּי טוֹב שְׂכָרִי — the Arabic is a fragment ('there is my rest, as the best reward is mine'); Hebrew joins the two lines into one clause so the couplet lands.
2:2 אֶזְרַח בְּכָבוֹד — 'I shall shine in glory'; זָרַח is the biblical verb for light breaking forth (Isa 60:1), which suits أَلْمَعُ better than a passive.
3:1 עִקְבוֹת חֵטְא יִמָּחוּ — 'the traces of sin shall be wiped out'; מָחָה is the biblical verb of blotting out (Ps 51:3), matching يَمَّحِي.
3:3 הַנִּצְחִי — 'the eternal [day]'; the adjective is post-biblical in this absolute use, but נֵצַח itself is biblical (Isa 34:10) and the line needs one word here.
